correctness.rationale: Exact face enumeration over all 2^12 subsets gives 120 forbidden triples and f-vector (12,66,100,30). The distance-two subcomplex is a connected closed surface with links 5-cycles and Euler characteristic two, hence S^2. Each of thirty new graph edges attaches with an explicit triangular free pair over the sphere; the remaining cells of dimension >=2 do not create pi1. Thirty unique tetrahedral free triangles collapse the remainder to a simply connected two-complex of Euler characteristic 22, hence wedge 21 S^2. Six distance-three edges occur in no triangle and each wedges on S^1. All critical finite assertions are directly checked by the embedded code; topological arguments prove the integral homotopy type.

originality.rationale: Direct comparisons distinguish the full geodesic general-position face system on the twelve-vertex icosahedral graph from ordinary independent sets, the two-independence complex, metric Rips complexes and distance-neighborhood nerves. The two accessible foundational primary full texts define/characterize general position but supply neither this icosahedral homotopy nor a dominating theorem from which the twenty-one 2-spheres follow. Available indexed searches found no covering calculation. The explicit twenty-one-sphere conclusion has more information than general-position extrema or face enumerators; unindexed equivalent results remain possible.

value.rationale: The icosahedral graph is a natural vertex-transitive polyhedral graph and the GP complex assembles all geodesic-general-position configurations rather than measuring only their maximum size. The 21 independent two-spheres are invisible in the known single two-sphere of its ordinary independence complex and cannot be inferred merely from face enumeration. The topological decomposition, including a spherical distance-two core and an exact 20-sphere contribution, is a meaningful structural boundary/benchmark for comparing graph-geodesic complexes. The claim is restricted honestly to one graph.
